Report on the pre-processing, the decomposition and the diagnostics

Source: R/sa_decomposition.R, R/sa_diagnostics.R, R/sa_preprocessing.R
sa_preprocessing.Rd

Functions to describe a seasonal adjustment model in a report:

sa_decomposition(
  x,
  digits = 3,
  decimal.mark = getOption("OutDec"),
  title_level = NULL
)

sa_diagnostics(
  x,
  tests = diagnostics_tests$id,
  digits = 3,
  decimal.mark = getOption("OutDec"),
  signif_stars = TRUE,
  var_decomposition = TRUE,
  title_level = NULL
)

sa_preprocessing(
  x,
  digits = 3,
  decimal.mark = getOption("OutDec"),
  signif_stars = TRUE,
  title_level = NULL,
  summary = TRUE,
  likelihood = TRUE,
  arima = TRUE,
  regression = TRUE
)

Arguments

x

a seasonal adjustment model: result of rjd3x13::x13(), rjd3tramoseats::tramoseats(), rjd3x13::jx13(), rjd3tramoseats::jtramoseats() or a SA-item read from a workspace (see rjd3workspace::read_sai() or rjd3workspace::read_workspace()). The pre-processing models (rjd3x13::regarima() and rjd3tramoseats::tramo()) are also supported by sa_preprocessing() and sa_diagnostics().

digits

number of digits used in the tables and in the text.

decimal.mark

the character used as decimal mark.

title_level

NULL (default) to print the titles in bold or an integer to print them as markdown headings of that level (e.g. title_level = 3 for ### Title).

tests

identifiers of the tests to print. By default all the available tests: "mean", "skewness", "kurtosis", "doornikhansen" (normality), "lb" (Ljung-Box), "seaslb" (Ljung-Box at seasonal lags), "lb2" (Ljung-Box on squared residuals), "seas.qstest.sa", "seas.ftest.sa", "seas.qstest.i", "seas.ftest.i" (residual seasonality on the seasonally adjusted series and on the irregular), "td.ftest.sa" and "td.ftest.i" (residual trading days effects).

signif_stars

boolean indicating if the significance stars should be added to the tables.

var_decomposition

boolean indicating if the table with the variance decomposition should be printed (only for seasonal adjustment models).

summary, likelihood, arima, regression

booleans indicating which parts of the pre-processing description should be printed.

Value

An object of class "rjd3report_block" (see print.rjd3report_block()).

Details

  • sa_preprocessing() describes the pre-processing (RegARIMA or TRAMO model): summary of the model, likelihood statistics, ARIMA and regression coefficients;

  • sa_decomposition() describes the decomposition (X-11 or SEATS);

  • sa_diagnostics() prints a table with the main diagnostics tests on the quality of the pre-processing and of the decomposition.

The functions return objects that are automatically rendered in a Quarto (or R Markdown) document, whatever the output format (HTML, PDF with LaTeX or Typst, Word...): it is no longer necessary to specify the output format nor to use the chunk option results: asis. The tables are built with tinytable. The objects can also be printed in the console.

See also

sa_report(), render_report().

Examples

y <- rjd3toolkit::ABS$X0.2.09.10.M
sa_x13 <- rjd3x13::x13(y)
sa_preprocessing(sa_x13)

sa_decomposition(sa_x13)
#> Decomposition (X-11)
#> 
#> Mode: multiplicative
#> 
#> Final filters: seasonal 3x5, Henderson 23 terms
#> 
#> 
#> +-----------+-------+------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
#> | Statistic | Value | Description                                                                                                                        |
#> +===========+=======+====================================================================================================================================+
#> | M-1       | 0.071 | The relative contribution of the irregular over three months span                                                                  |
#> +-----------+-------+------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
#> | M-2       | 0.075 | The relative contribution of the irregular component to the stationary portion of the variance                                     |
#> +-----------+-------+------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
#> | M-3       | 2.119 | The amount of period to period change in the irregular component as compared to the amount of period to period change in the trend |
#> +-----------+-------+------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
#> | M-4       | 0.134 | The amount of autocorrelation in the irregular as described by the average duration of run                                         |
#> +-----------+-------+------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
#> | M-5       | 1.632 | The number of periods it takes the change in the trend to surpass the amount of change in the irregular                            |
#> +-----------+-------+------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+

#> +-----------+-------+------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
#> | M-7       | 0.053 | The amount of moving seasonality present relative to the amount of stable seasonality                                              |
#> +-----------+-------+------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
#> | M-8       | 0.163 | The size of the fluctuations in the seasonal component throughout the whole series                                                 |
#> +-----------+-------+------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
#> | M-9       | 0.050 | The average linear movement in the seasonal component throughout the whole series                                                  |
#> +-----------+-------+------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
#> | M-10      | 0.146 | The size of the fluctuations in the seasonal component in the recent years                                                         |
#> +-----------+-------+------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
#> | M-11      | 0.143 | The average linear movement in the seasonal component in the recent years                                                          |
#> +-----------+-------+------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------+
#> | Q         | 0.465 | Weighted average of the M-statistics                                                                                               |

sa_ts <- rjd3tramoseats::tramoseats(y)
sa_decomposition(sa_ts)
#> Decomposition (SEATS)
#> 
#> Mode: multiplicative
#> 
#> | Component | AR | Differencing | MA | Innovation variance |
#> |:--|:--|:--|:--|--:|
#> | Model | 1 | 1 - B - B^{12} + B^{13} | 1 - 0.828B - 0.426B^{12} + 0.352B^{13} | 1.000 |
#> | Trend | 1 | 1 - 2B + B^{2} | 1 + 0.064B - 0.936B^{2} | 0.004 |
#> | Seasonal | 1 | 1 + B + \cdots + B^{11} | 1 + 0.620B + 0.312B^{2} + 0.073B^{3} - 0.103B^{4} - 0.222B^{5} - 0.293B^{6} - 0.324B^{7} - 0.322B^{8} - 0.295B^{9} - 0.251B^{10} - 0.195B^{11} | 0.146 |
#> | Irregular | 1 | 1 | 1 | 0.385 |
#> | Seasonally adjusted | 1 | 1 - 2B + B^{2} | 1 - 1.761B + 0.772B^{2} | 0.493 |
#> 
#> : SEATS canonical decomposition (polynomials in the backshift operator B)
#>
